entry.title: Hermann Prey - Rossini: Il Barbiere di Siviglia: Largo al Factotum (Excerpt)

media:group.media:title: Hermann Prey - Rossini: Il Barbiere di Siviglia: Largo al Factotum (Excerpt)
media:group.media:description:
Watch Hermann Prey sing Figaro’s famous entrance aria “Largo al factotum” from Rossini’s 'Il barbiere di Siviglia', accompanied by the Orchestra del Teatro alla Scala under Claudio Abbado.
This performance is taken from Jean-Pierre Ponnelle’s acclaimed 1972 film adaptation of Rossini’s comic opera, based on his Salzburg staging and featuring the Chorus and Orchestra of La Scala, Milan.
Watch the full opera on our streaming service STAGE+: https://www.stage-plus.com/video/vod_concert_APNM8GRFDPHMASJKBSQ3IC8
For more than two centuries, Rossini's 1816 adaptation of Beaumarchais's The Barber of Seville has delighted, amused and astonished audiences around the world. It's a true comic classic and in Figaro, its witty, endlessly resourceful title character, Rossini gave opera one of its most engaging and charismatic heroes. Fittingly, this 1972 film version united two equally innovative and energetic young talents – the French director Jean-Pierre Ponnelle and conductor Claudio Abbado – in an exuberant, handsome-looking production based on Ponnelle's classic Salzburg staging, and recorded using the forces of La Scala, Milan. Hermann Prey, Teresa Berganza and Luigi Alva all star in this sparkling account of the supreme bel canto comedy.
Hermann Prey, Chorus and orchestra of La Scala, Claudio Abbado - Rossini: Il Barbiere di Siviglia: Largo al Factotum (Excerpt)

media:group.media:title: Hildur Guðnadóttir - Blind Sarabande
media:group.media:description:
Watch award-winning Icelandic composer Hildur Guðnadóttir perform 'Blind Sarabande' from her new album 'This Will Be Us'. Discover the album at https://dg.lnk.to/ThisWillBeUs
Watch the premiere of the full concert from which this video is taken and presenting music from the full album on our streaming service STAGE+: https://www.stage-plus.com/de/video/live_concert_9HKNCPA3DTN66PBIEHFJ2D1H74
Hildur Guðnadóttir’s album 'This Will Be Us' is a deeply personal reflection on memory, connection and the people who shape us. On it, Guðnadóttir revisits music from across her catalogue alongside two new compositions. The album reimagines works once recorded in solitude through the expansive voice of orchestra, for which she is joined by conductor and longtime collaborator Robert Ames and the DSO Berlin. The album cover artwork was created by acclaimed Icelandic-Danish artist Ólafur Elíasson, with liner notes by Hildur herself and filmmaker Sarah Polley.
“When I was recording, trying to be a one-person string orchestra, I always dreamed of having more people playing with me. Now, twenty years later, I decided to make that dream come true – to give that young person the anniversary gift of hearing her music played by an orchestra,” says Guðnadóttir.
The full album is released digitally, on CD and on vinyl. Order the CD and LP editions in the DG Store: https://store.deutschegrammophon.com/en-de/collections/hildur-gudnadottir

entry.title: Bryn Terfel, Claudio Abbado - Wagner: Wotan's Farewell (from Die Walküre, Excerpt)

media:group.media:title: Bryn Terfel, Claudio Abbado - Wagner: Wotan's Farewell (from Die Walküre, Excerpt)
media:group.media:description:
Watch Bryn Terfel sing Wotan’s both powerful and touching farewell from Wagner’s 'Die Walküre' together with Claudio Abbado and the Lucerne Festival Orchestra.
We celebrate Bryn Terfel on his birthday on 9 November. This performance comes from the inaugural concert of Abbado’s Lucerne Festival Orchestra in 2003, where Terfel joined the newly formed ensemble for the final scene of Wagner’s 'Die Walküre'.
Watch the full concert on our streaming service STAGE+: https://www.stage-plus.com/video/vod_concert_APNM8GRFDPHMASJKBSOJAE0
Claudio Abbado had loved the music of Claude Debussy since his childhood, so it was no surprise that he chose music by the French composer for the first concert of his Lucerne Festival Orchestra. In addition to the vivid "symphonic sketches" of La mer, which shimmers in a thousand moods and colours before culminating in a grand finale, the concert features the suite from the much lesser-known mystery play Le Martyre de Saint Sébastien, a collaboration with the Italian writer Gabriele D'Annunzio. Completing the programme, superstar bass-baritone Bryn Terfel, one of Abbado's favorite singers, lends his powerful voice to the moving final scene from Wagner's Die Walküre.
Bryn Terfel, Luzern Festival Orchestra, Claudio Abbado - Wagner: Wotan's Farewell (from Die Walküre, Excerpt)

entry.title: Frederika von Stade, Claudio Abbado - Rossini: La Cenerentola: “Non più mesta” (Excerpt)

media:group.media:title: Frederika von Stade, Claudio Abbado - Rossini: La Cenerentola: “Non più mesta” (Excerpt)
media:group.media:description:
Watch Frederica von Stade sing the dazzling “Non più mesta” as Angelina (Cinderella) in Rossini’s 'La Cenerentola', with the Coro and Orchestra del Teatro alla Scala under Claudio Abbado.
This performance is taken from Jean-Pierre Ponnelle’s celebrated 1981 film of Rossini’s opera, with Abbado conducting the forces of La Scala.
Watch the full opera on our streaming service STAGE+: https://www.stage-plus.com/video/vod_concert_APNM8GRFDPHMASJKBSQ3ICG
Rossini's La Cenerentola is an operatic fairy tale with a remarkably modern edge: there are no fairy godmothers or supernatural transformations, and the magic that drives the story is the power of compassionate love. It was a perfect subject for the innovative French director Jean-Pierre Ponnelle, and this enchanting filmed version from 1981 combines the production values of Ponnelle's La Scala staging (the young Claudio Abbado strikes sparks in the pit) with the visual possibilities of a movie (it was filmed in Vienna). Ponnelle updates the action to Rossini's own era, and with Frederica von Stade in the title role, the results are as refreshing as they are delightful.

media:group.media:description:
With ‘Immortal – Winter Edition’, David Garrett presents a limited 2-CD edition of his new album. Alongside the 25-track Deluxe Edition of ‘Immortal’, a second CD brings together 11 winter-themed recordings personally chosen by David from different stages of his career.
A collection made for quiet evenings, frosted landscapes and the atmosphere of winter.
